note: No visibility. The tier is fixed for the life of the room, so a community never chooses it on an administrator's behalf.
No reason. Creating a room the community owns is an act of the community, and the audit trail records why.
A room identifier supplied by the caller. The community's VTA mints the room's identity; an administrator naming one would be asking the community to own a DID whose key it does not hold.
An empty description. A room without one omits the member; an empty string would display as a description that says nothing.
A tag that is not an identifier. Tags are for filtering, so they are short lower-case identifiers; prose belongs in `description`.
Bare/unnamespaced ext key — SPEC §4.5.1 requires every immediate child of ext to be reverse-DNS namespaced.
